items.q: An angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is x. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with diameter AB. A point C on the circumference is joined to A and B, and the angle at C is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: AB is a diameter of the circle.
hints: Recall the circle theorem for an angle subtended by a diameter.
The angle in a semicircle is always a right angle.

items.q: A triangle in a semicircle has one angle 35° and the angle in the semicircle. Find the third angle.
items.imageAlt: A circle with diameter AB and a point C on the circumference. The angle at C is marked as a right angle, the angle at A is marked 35 degrees, and the angle at B is unknown.
items.imageCaption: AB is a diameter of the circle.
hints: The angle in the semicircle is 90°; angles in a triangle sum to 180°.

items.q: If one non-right angle in a semicircle triangle is 28°, find the other.
items.imageAlt: A circle with diameter AB and a point C on the circumference. The angle at C is marked as a right angle, the angle at A is marked 28 degrees, and the angle at B is unknown.
items.imageCaption: AB is a diameter of the circle.
hints: The angle in the semicircle is 90°; angles in a triangle sum to 180°.

items.q: True or false: the angle in a semicircle is always a right angle.
hints: Recall the circle theorem for an angle subtended by a diameter.
Any angle at the circumference standing on a diameter is 90°.
True

items.q: A semicircle triangle has angles 90°, 41°, and x. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with diameter AB and a point C on the circumference. The angle at C is marked as a right angle, the angle at A is marked 41 degrees, and the angle at B is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: AB is a diameter of the circle.
hints: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°.

items.q: An angle in a semicircle triangle is 90°. What theorem is this?
hints: Recall the name of the circle theorem for a right angle standing on a diameter.
This is the 'angle in a semicircle' theorem.
Angle in a semicircle

items.q: AB is the diameter of a circle, with AB = 13 cm. C is a point on the circumference, with AC = 5 cm. Find the length of BC.
items.imageAlt: A circle with diameter AB marked 13 cm. Point C is on the circumference, forming a triangle with A and B. The angle at C is marked with a right angle symbol. AC is marked 5 cm. BC is unknown, to be found.
items.imageCaption: AB is a diameter.
hints: Since AB is a diameter, the angle at C is a right angle (angle in a semicircle theorem) — this makes triangle ACB right-angled at C, so use Pythagoras' theorem.

items.q: An angle at the centre is 80°. Find the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. Points A and B are on the circumference. The angle at O is marked 80 degrees. Point C is on the circumference on the far arc, and the angle at C is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: O is the centre of the circle.
hints: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

items.q: An angle at the circumference is 35°. Find the angle at the centre on the same arc.
hints: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

items.q: The centre angle is double which other angle?
hints: Recall the two angles this circle theorem compares.
It relates the angle at the centre to the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
Angle at the circumference

items.q: An angle at the centre is 124°. Find the matching circumference angle.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. Points A and B are on the circumference on the left. The angle at O is marked 124 degrees. Point C is on the circumference at the bottom right, and the angle at C is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: O is the centre of the circle.
hints: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

items.q: A circumference angle is 48°. Find the matching centre angle.
hints: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

items.q: If the centre angle is x and the circumference angle is 33°, find x.
hints: The angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

items.q: The reflex angle at the centre is 260°. Find the angle at the circumference on the corresponding minor arc.
hints: Find the non-reflex angle at the centre first, then halve it.
360 - 260 = 100, and the circumference angle is half of that.

items.q: O is the centre of a circle. A and B are points on the circumference, and OA = OB (radii). Angle OAB = 35°. C is another point on the circumference, on the major arc AB. Find angle ACB.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. Points A and B are on the circumference, joined to O by radii. The angle at A between OA and AB is marked 35 degrees. Point C is on the major arc AB, and the angle ACB is marked x degrees, the unknown to find.
items.imageCaption: OA and OB are radii.
hints: OA and OB are both radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles — angle OBA = angle OAB = 35°.
Angle AOB = 180 - 35 - 35 = 110° (angle sum of a triangle). Then use the angle at the centre theorem: angle ACB = 110 / 2.

items.q: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are x and 112°. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with cyclic quadrilateral ABCD inscribed. The angle at A is marked x degrees. The opposite angle at C is marked 112 degrees.
items.imageCaption: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.
hints: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

items.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite angles 3x and 96°. Find x.
hints: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

items.q: One angle in a cyclic quadrilateral is 71°. Find the opposite angle.
items.imageAlt: A circle with cyclic quadrilateral ABCD inscribed, positioned differently than the other cyclic quadrilateral diagram. The angle at A is marked 71 degrees. The opposite angle at C is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.
hints: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

items.q: True or false: opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.
hints: Recall the circle theorem for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.
Opposite angles are supplementary in a cyclic quadrilateral.
True

items.q: Opposite angles are x and x + 24 in a cyclic quadrilateral. Find x.
hints: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

items.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has opposite angles 84° and y. Find y.
hints: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

items.q: A, B, C, D are points on a circle, centre O. Angle BOD = 150° and angle ADB = 35°. Work out the size of angle ABD, giving a reason for each stage of your working.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O and cyclic quadrilateral ABCD inscribed. The angle at O between radii OB and OD is marked 150 degrees. Diagonal BD is drawn. Inside triangle ABD, the angle at D is marked 35 degrees, and the angle at B is marked x degrees, the unknown to find.
items.imageCaption: O is the centre of the circle.
hints: This combines three theorems. First, find angle BCD using the angle at the centre theorem (the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc).

Angle BCD = 150 / 2 = 75°. Then use the cyclic quadrilateral theorem (opposite angles sum to 180°) to find angle BAD = 180 - 75 = 105°. Finally, in triangle ABD, use the angle sum of a triangle (180°) with the given angle ADB = 35° to find angle ABD.

items.q: Angles in the same segment are 42° and x. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with points A and B on the circumference. Points C and D are on the major arc, in the same segment. The angle at C is marked 42 degrees. The angle at D is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: C and D are in the same segment.
hints: Angles in the same segment, standing on the same arc, are equal.

items.q: True or false: angles in the same segment are equal.
hints: Recall the circle theorem for angles subtended by the same arc, from the same side.
All such angles in the same segment are equal to each other.
True

items.q: An angle in one segment is 57°. Find the matching angle in the same segment.
items.imageAlt: A circle with points A and B on the circumference, positioned differently than the other same-segment diagram. Points C and D are on the major arc below, in the same segment. The angle at C is marked 57 degrees. The angle at D is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: C and D are in the same segment.
hints: Angles in the same segment, standing on the same arc, are equal.
The matching angle is also 57°.

items.q: Angles in the same segment are 3x and 84°. Find x.
hints: Angles in the same segment, standing on the same arc, are equal.

items.q: If one same-segment angle is 31°, what is the other?
hints: Angles in the same segment, standing on the same arc, are equal.
The other angle is also 31°.

items.q: Angles in the same segment are x and x + 7. Is this possible?
hints: Angles in the same segment must be equal — check whether the two expressions can ever match.
x = x + 7 has no solution, since that would require 0 = 7.
No

items.q: A, B, C, D are points on a circle. A and D are in the same segment relative to chord BC. Angle BAC = 42°. Angle DBC = 55°. Find angle BCD.
items.imageAlt: A circle with chord BC. Points A and D are both on the same major arc, in the same segment. The angle BAC at A is marked 42 degrees. The angle DBC at B is marked 55 degrees. The angle BCD at C is marked x degrees, the unknown to find.
items.imageCaption: A and D are in the same segment.
hints: A and D are in the same segment, so angle BDC = angle BAC = 42° (angles in the same segment theorem).
In triangle BDC, use the angle sum of a triangle: angle BCD = 180 - 42 - 55.

items.q: The angle between a tangent and chord is 48°. Find the angle in the alternate segment.
items.imageAlt: A circle with a tangent line touching at point A. Chord AB is drawn from A. The angle between the tangent and the chord is marked 48 degrees. Point C is on the far arc, and the angle ACB in the alternate segment is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: The line at A is a tangent.
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.
The alternate segment angle is also 48°.

items.q: A tangent-chord angle is x and the alternate segment angle is 63°. Find x.
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.

items.q: True or false: the angle between a tangent and chord equals the angle in the alternate segment.
hints: Recall the alternate segment theorem.
The tangent-chord angle always equals the angle in the alternate segment.
True

items.q: The alternate segment angle is 35°. Find the tangent-chord angle.
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.
The tangent-chord angle is also 35°.

items.q: A tangent-chord angle is 2x and the alternate segment angle is 74°. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with a tangent line touching at point A, positioned differently than the other alternate segment diagram. Chord AB is drawn from A. The angle between the tangent and the chord is marked 2x. Point C is on the far arc, and the angle ACB in the alternate segment is marked 74 degrees.
items.imageCaption: The line at A is a tangent.
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.

items.q: The tangent-chord angle is 90°. What is the alternate segment angle?
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.
The alternate segment angle is also 90°.

items.q: TQ is a chord of a circle, and PT is a tangent at T. The angle between the tangent and the chord is 65°. R is a point on the far arc. Angle TQR = 45°. Find angle QTR.
items.imageAlt: A circle with a tangent line touching at point T. Chord TQ is drawn, with the tangent-chord angle marked 65 degrees. R is a point on the far arc, with lines TR and QR drawn. The angle at Q inside triangle TQR is marked 45 degrees. The angle at T inside triangle TQR is marked x degrees, the unknown to find.
items.imageCaption: The line at T is a tangent.
hints: The alternate segment theorem: the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment, so angle TRQ = 65°.
In triangle TQR, use the angle sum of a triangle: angle QTR = 180 - 65 - 45.

items.q: What angle does a radius make with a tangent at the point of contact?
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. A radius OA is drawn to point A on the circumference. A tangent line touches the circle at A, meeting the radius at a right angle.
items.imageCaption: OA is a radius.
hints: Recall the circle theorem about tangents and radii.
A radius always meets a tangent at a right angle at the point of contact.

items.q: A tangent and radius meet at angle x. Find x.
hints: Recall the circle theorem about tangents and radii.
A radius always meets a tangent at a right angle at the point of contact.

items.q: True or false: a radius is perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact.
hints: Recall the circle theorem about tangents and radii.
This is always true at the point where the tangent touches the circle.
True

items.q: A tangent touches a circle at P. What is angle OPT if OP is a radius?
hints: Recall the circle theorem about tangents and radii — O is the centre, P is the point of contact.
The radius OP always meets the tangent at a right angle.

items.q: If a line is tangent to a circle, what is its angle to the radius there?
hints: Recall the circle theorem about tangents and radii.
A tangent always meets the radius at the point of contact at a right angle.

items.q: A radius and tangent form a right angle. Which theorem is this?
hints: Recall the name of this circle theorem.
This is the 'radius perpendicular to tangent' theorem.
Radius perpendicular to tangent

items.q: OA is a radius and AT is a tangent at A. If angle AOT = 55°, find angle OTA.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. OA is a radius to point A. AT is a tangent at A, meeting the radius at a right angle. T is a point along the tangent line. Angle AOT is marked 55 degrees, and angle OTA is marked x degrees.
items.imageCaption: AT is a tangent at A.
hints: The radius meets the tangent at 90° — use the angle sum of the triangle OAT.
Angle OAT = 90°, so angle OTA = 180 - 90 - 55.

items.q: A circle has centre O and radius 5 cm. T is an external point with OT = 13 cm. AT is a tangent to the circle at A. Find the length of AT.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. Radius OA is marked 5 cm. AT is a tangent at A, meeting the radius at a right angle. T is an external point, and OT is marked 13 cm. AT is unknown, to be found.
items.imageCaption: AT is a tangent at A.
hints: The radius meets the tangent at a right angle, so triangle OAT is right-angled at A — use Pythagoras' theorem.

items.q: Tangents from the same external point are lengths x and 9. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. From an external point T, two tangent lines touch the circle at points A and B. Segment TA is marked x. Segment TB is marked 9.
items.imageCaption: TA and TB are tangents from T.
hints: Two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length.

items.q: Two tangents from the same point have lengths 3x and 21. Find x.
hints: Two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length.

items.q: True or false: tangents from the same point are equal in length.
hints: Recall the circle theorem about two tangents from one external point.
The two tangent lengths are always equal.
True

items.q: Tangents from one external point are x + 2 and 11. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O, positioned differently than the other tangents-from-a-point diagram. From an external point T, two tangent lines touch the circle at points A and B. Segment TA is marked x plus 2. Segment TB is marked 11.
items.imageCaption: TA and TB are tangents from T.
hints: Two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length.

items.q: If one tangent from an external point is 14, what is the other?
hints: Two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length.
The other tangent is also 14.

items.q: Tangents from the same point are 5x - 1 and 19. Find x.
hints: Two tangents drawn from the same external point are always equal in length.

items.q: From an external point T, two tangents TA and TB touch a circle with centre O, at points A and B. Angle ATB = 50°. Find angle AOB.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O. From an external point T, two tangent lines touch the circle at points A and B, with right angles marked where each tangent meets its radius. The angle at T is marked 50 degrees. The angle at O is marked x degrees, the unknown to find.
items.imageCaption: TA and TB are tangents.
hints: Each radius meets its tangent at a right angle (radius perpendicular to tangent theorem), giving quadrilateral OATB two right angles, at A and B.
Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°: angle AOB = 360 - 90 - 90 - 50.

items.q: A radius meets a chord at 90°. What else does it do to the chord?
hints: Recall the second half of this circle theorem, beyond the right angle.
A perpendicular radius doesn't just meet the chord at 90° — it also cuts it exactly in half.
Bisects it

items.q: A chord is 16 cm long. A perpendicular radius meets it. Find half the chord.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O and a chord AB. A perpendicular line from O meets the chord at its midpoint M. The chord AB is 16 cm long, and each half AM and MB is unknown.
items.imageCaption: AB = 16 cm.
hints: A perpendicular radius bisects the chord — divide the chord length by 2.

items.q: True or false: a perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
hints: Recall the circle theorem about a radius perpendicular to a chord.
The perpendicular from the centre always cuts the chord into two equal halves.
True

items.q: Half a bisected chord is 6 cm. Find the full chord.
hints: Reverse the bisection by doubling the half.

items.q: A radius is perpendicular to a 20 cm chord. Find each half.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O and a vertical chord AB, positioned differently than the other radius-chord diagram. A perpendicular line from O meets the chord at its midpoint M. The chord AB is 20 cm long, and each half AM and MB is unknown.
items.imageCaption: AB = 20 cm.
hints: A perpendicular radius bisects the chord — divide the chord length by 2.

items.q: Which theorem states that a perpendicular radius bisects a chord?
items.a: Radius perpendicular to chord bisects chord
hints: Recall the name of this circle theorem.
This is the 'radius perpendicular to chord bisects chord' theorem.
Radius perpendicular to chord bisects chord

items.q: A chord AB is drawn in a circle, centre O, with radius 10 cm. The perpendicular distance from O to the chord is 6 cm. Find the length of AB.
items.imageAlt: A circle with centre O, radius 10 cm, and a chord AB. A perpendicular line from O meets the chord at its midpoint M, marked 6 cm. The radius OA is drawn, forming a right-angled triangle. AB is unknown, to be found.
items.imageCaption: O is the centre of the circle.
hints: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, forming a right-angled triangle OMA with the radius as the hypotenuse — use Pythagoras' theorem to find half the chord.
AM² = OA² - OM² = 10² - 6² = 100 - 36 = 64, so AM = 8. The full chord AB is double this.

items.q: Two chords intersect. One has segments 3 and 8, the other has segments 4 and x. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with two chords AB and CD crossing inside the circle at point P. Segment PA is marked 3, segment PB is marked 8, segment PC is marked 4, and segment PD is marked x.
items.imageCaption: AB and CD cross at P.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's.

items.q: Two intersecting chords have segments 5 and 6 on one chord, and 3 and x on the other. Find x.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's.

items.q: If one chord has segments 2 and 9 and the other 3 and x, find x.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's.

items.q: True or false: for intersecting chords, segment product equals segment product.
hints: Recall the intersecting chord theorem.
The product of the two segments of one chord equals the product of the two segments of the other.
True

items.q: Chords intersect with segments 4 and 7, and 2 and x. Find x.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's.

items.q: Chords intersect with segments 6 and 10, and 5 and x. Find x.
items.imageAlt: A circle with two chords AB and CD crossing inside the circle at point P, positioned differently than the other intersecting chords diagram. Segment PA is marked 6, segment PB is marked 10, segment PC is marked 5, and segment PD is marked x.
items.imageCaption: AB and CD cross at P.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's.

items.q: Two chords intersect. One has segments x and x+2, the other has segments 4 and 6. Find x.
hints: For intersecting chords, the product of one chord's segments equals the product of the other's — this time it gives a quadratic in x.
x(x + 2) = 4 x 6, so x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0, which factorises to (x + 6)(x - 4) = 0.

items.q: Two chords AB and CD intersect at point P inside a circle. AP = 4, PB = 9, and CP = 6. Find the length of CD.
items.imageAlt: A circle with two chords AB and CD crossing inside the circle at point P. Segment PA is marked 4, segment PB is marked 9, segment PC is marked 6, and segment PD is unknown, to be found.
items.imageCaption: AB and CD cross at P.
hints: First find PD using the intersecting chord theorem: AP × PB = CP × PD.
4 × 9 = 6 × PD, so 36 = 6 × PD, giving PD = 6. Then CD = CP + PD.
